reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in reformulating finite-horizon Kelly optimization as a quantile-maximization problem over multinomial outcome spaces. Terminal wealth is expressed as X_n(W) = ∏ W_i^{N_i}, where N follows a multinomial distribution. Outcome space is partitioned into 'chambers' based on fixed wealth orderings. Within each chamber, the α-quantile of terminal wealth becomes a monomial in N, termed the 'active quantile monomial'. Maximizing this monomial yields a 'shadow-Kelly' solution for the empirical distribution of outcomes in that chamber. Global optimization is achieved by enumerating all chambers and solving their respective shadow-Kelly problems. This approach avoids the asymptotic assumptions of classical Kelly, targeting specific quantiles like median wealth directly. The method leverages geometric properties of Arrow–Debreu wealth profiles to maintain tractability despite finite horizons. Failure modes include combinatorial explosion in chamber enumeration and sensitivity to misestimated p and q, which propagate into shadow-Kelly points.
